Four signals share one portfolio risk model | 04 | Sleeve | Signal budget | Directional information | Daily price trend | 30% | Sign of trailing 252-day return | Economic trend | 20% | Five predefined economic themes | Negative skew | 20% | Relative skewness within each asset class | Extra Trees (42) | 30% | Probability of a positive next-month return | 10% predicted volatility for the blended portfolio | Full rebalance every 21 business days. No gross, net, or asset-class caps. | Budgets combine proposed weights. They are not risk contributions. Missing sleeve budgets go to price trend.

Economic trend uses five predefined themes | 05 | Theme | Dated input | Construction | Growth | INDPRO.csv | Change in 12-month production growth | Inflation | CPIAUCSL.csv | Change in 12-month CPI inflation | Monetary policy | GS2.csv | 12-month change in two-year yield | Trade | Currency-futures returns | Average trailing 12-month return | Risk environment | BAA10Y.csv and equity futures | Opposite credit-spread change plus equity trend | Fixed asset-class directions and 3-month smoothing

Our factor library goes beyond momentum | 06 | 31 raw factors = 25 price-path measures + 6 peer / residual measures | Trend & price path  |  10 | TSMOM; skip-month momentum; acceleration; persistence | Trend efficiency; mean / vol; distance to high | Drawdown; positive-month share; median / vol | Reversal  |  3 | 1-month reversal; 3-month reversal | Long-horizon reversal (months 36 to 12) | Volatility & downside  |  5 | Low volatility; low downside / upside risk | 3-to-12-month volatility compression | Low volatility of volatility | Tail shape  |  6 | Negative skew; low kurtosis; low maximum return | Mild worst return; low tail loss; risk asymmetry | Seasonality  |  1 | Average same-calendar-month return | from the previous five years | Peer & residual information  |  6 | Low peer beta / correlation; low residual volatility | Residual momentum; peer-relative reversal | Peer-relative skip-month momentum | 31 raw factors generate 66 candidate inputs; train-only IC + t screening retains 42. Exact names are in speaker notes.

Two roles: ML features and negative skew | 07 | The screened 42-input classifier and the 20% negative-skew sleeve serve different roles | Model representation: 42 inputs | 20 raw + 18 ranks + 4 class flags | Candidate pool: 31 raw + 31 ranks + 4 class flags. | Train only: |mean IC| ≥ 0.01 and |HAC t| ≥ 1.96. | Retain 20 raw factors + 18 ranks + 4 class flags. | Fix the 42-input list; refit the model before 2015. | Standalone negative skew: 20% | 1  Compute negative skew from 12 monthly returns. | 2  Rank within class; center ranks around zero. | 3  Long relatively more negative-skew markets; short less negative-skew peers. | 4  Divide by volatility; normalize forecast risk. | Screening changes ML inputs only. The independent 20% negative-skew sleeve is unchanged; no individual alpha claim.

From historical returns to the final portfolio | 08 | Monthly forecasts feed a daily-risk portfolio traded every 21 business days | 1  Historical returns | Monthly price paths | and same-class peer returns | → | 2  Factors + class ranks | 66 candidates → 42 inputs | Train-only IC + HAC t filter | → | 3  Extra Trees | 200 trees fitted on 42 inputs | learn nonlinear combinations | 4  Next-month probability | p = P(next monthly return > 0) | This is a forecast, not a return | → | 5  Direction → position | direction = 2p − 1 | Divide by volatility; risk-normalize | → | 6  Final combination | 30% trend + 20% macro | + 20% skew + 30% ML | Example: p = 0.65 → direction +0.30; p = 0.50 → 0; p = 0.35 → −0.30 | Blend → 10% ex-ante risk scaling → full 21-business-day rebalance. The direction score is not a final NAV weight. | 3 → 4: the model output becomes a probability, then a proposed position.

Chronological fits keep future labels out | 09 | Screen 42 inputs before 2005; refit the model before 2015; freeze both thereafter | Before 2005 | Screen inputs + train | |mean IC| ≥ 0.01; |HAC t| ≥ 1.96. | Use labels known before the | first Dec-2004 formation. | → | 2005–2014 | Freeze the first fit | Validate the frozen 42-input | model on 2005–2014. | No later labels enter this fit. | → | Before 2015 → later | Refit once, then freeze | Keep the same 42-input list. | Refit with pre-2015 labels; | freeze for the later interval. | Model: 200 trees  |  depth ≤ 6  |  min leaf = 30  |  max features = 0.7 | Before 2005 there is no active ML forecast; its 30% budget returns to price trend. | Causal fitting prevents label leakage. It does not make repeatedly viewed later returns an untouched holdout.

Final specification and selection rationale | 10 | A fixed, reproducible specification; research alternatives remain separate | Retained in the final submission | Negative skew: interpretable peer-selection sleeve (20%). | ET42: train IC + t-screened inputs (30%). | Fixed 30 / 20 / 20 / 30 budgets; 10% ex-ante scaling. | Full rebalance; no exposure caps. | Compared in the research | IC-only 56 inputs; IC + t fixed 42 inputs. | Other models, learned weights and slower execution. | Adding both optimizers: later Sharpe 0.3057. | Keep fixed budgets / full rebalance: 0.3567. | 42 vs baseline — IS: 1.2831 vs 1.2225; later: 0.3567 vs 0.2430 | Fixed 42-input policy: fewer inputs, similar IS Sharpe and a small later-period improvement over ET66. | The 42-input version was selected after later results were viewed. Differences remain within sampling uncertainty.
